nl_text:
The database schema named rschema_0083 consists of three tables: Author, Category, and Article.
The Author table has three columns: Author_ID, which is the primary key and of type INTEGER, Email, which is of type VARCHAR(255), and Name, also of type VARCHAR(255).
The Category table has two columns: Category_ID, which is the primary key and of type INTEGER, and Name, of type VARCHAR(255).
The Article table has four columns: Article_ID, which is the primary key and of type INTEGER, Author_ID, of type INTEGER, Category_ID, of type INTEGER, and Name, of type VARCHAR(255). The Author_ID and Category_ID columns are foreign keys referencing the Author and Category tables respectively. This schema represents a many-to-many relationship between the Author and Category tables and a one-to-many relationship between the Author and Article tables.
gold_question: The business requirement description for the blog management system: A company plans to develop a blog or content management system to manage articles, authors, and category information. The system shall support the creation, editing, and deletion of articles, recording the Article ID, Name, Author ID, and Category ID. It shall associate author and category information through the Author ID and Category ID fields respectively, and support querying articles by author or category. An article may belong to multiple categories. The system shall record the category name and assign it a Category ID. The system shall also record basic information about authors, including the Author ID, Name, and Email.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0083
CREATE TABLE `author` (
  `author_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`author_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `category` (
  `category_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`category_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `article` (
  `article_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `author_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `category_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`article_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `article_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`author_id`) REFERENCES `author` (`author_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `article_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`category_id`) REFERENCES `category` (`category_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
